assumptions: Every reachable vertex is a key in the adjacency dictionary (the code indexes self.vertices[vertex]); start_vertex is valid; adjacency lists are the graph representation; each adjacency entry counts toward E; set operations and queue put/get are expected/amortized O(1).
input_size: V = number of reachable vertices; E = adjacency entries scanned from reachable vertices; n = V + E.
rationale: Time: BFS marks a vertex visited before enqueueing, so each reachable vertex is enqueued and removed once. Its adjacency list is scanned once; total work is O(V + E). Score with n = V + E. Auxiliary space: The visited set and queue contain at most O(V) reachable vertices. The returned visited set is the result; counting it as working storage does not change the O(V) bound. Owner review: Confirmed against source: visited.add occurs in the same branch as queue.put, so every reachable vertex is enqueued once at most. Every reachable adjacency entry is scanned once; time O(V + E), space O(V), and the queue holds at most V vertices.

assumptions: Score the bottom-up entrypoint only; character comparison and table access are O(1); m and k may independently be zero or larger; N=max(m,k); retain boundary-cell work in the exact bound.

rationale: Time: The implementation fills every cell of an (m+1) by (k+1) table, including boundary rows and columns. The complete bound is O((m+1)(k+1)); this remains valid when either input is empty. With N=max(m,k), the worst-case class is O(N^2). Auxiliary space: The implementation allocates an (m+1) by (k+1) table. The complete space bound is O((m+1)(k+1)), including empty-input cases; its worst case for N=max(m,k) is O(N^2). Owner review: Confirmed against source: the full (m+1) by (n+1) table is allocated and every cell is filled, including boundaries for empty strings. Time and space are O((m+1)(k+1)), worst case O(N^2). For the label, k = len(word2); the code names the second length n.

assumptions: Character access is O(1); treat ArrayList append as amortized O(1); k>0 for a non-early-return run; matching output is excluded from auxiliary space; the helper computePrefixFunction is part of the analyzed operation.

assumptions: a is non-empty because the implementation reads a[0]; integer arithmetic is treated as O(1); n=a.length.

rationale: Time: The enhanced for-loop visits each array element once and performs constant work per element. Initialization and final comparison are constant time. Owner review: Confirmed against source: one pass with scalar state gives O(n) time and O(1) space. The final predictedAnswer comparison is constant work. assumptions: Input is a Python string; dictionary operations are expected O(1); n is its length and U is the number of distinct characters.
input_size: n = len(input_string); U = number of distinct characters in it.
rationale: Time: The for-loop visits each character once. Dictionary lookup/update is expected O(1), and left only moves forward; total time is O(n). Auxiliary space: The character-index dictionary stores at most one entry for each distinct character seen, so it uses O(U) space, bounded by O(n). Owner review: Confirmed against source: left only moves forward, so the scan is O(n) expected time with expected O(1) dictionary operations. The map holds at most U distinct characters, so auxiliary space is O(U), U <= n. Type checking and the empty-string guard are O(1).

assumptions: Input is a sorted Python list and target comparisons are O(1). Count slice copies as auxiliary storage while recursive frames retain their arguments; exclude the input and returned scalar.
input_size: n = len(a_list); assume O(1) element comparisons.
rationale: Time: Each call performs a slice copy of the remaining list before recursing. Across levels, copied lengths form a geometric sum n + n/2 + n/4 + ... = O(n), which dominates the O(log n) comparisons and calls. Auxiliary space: The recursive stack alone is O(log n), but active sliced lists across the recursive calls have geometrically decreasing lengths whose total is O(n); auxiliary space is therefore O(n). Owner review: The first call copies at most n/2 elements, the next n/4, and so on, so time is O(n). Python has no tail-call elimination, so every slice stays alive as an argument to its callee, and the live slices sum to O(n). This assumes list input. Slicing a range, as some doctests do, is O(1), but the stated assumption covers that.

assumptions: Input is a mutable list; comparisons and swaps are O(1). Count recursion stack as auxiliary space and exclude the input list.
input_size: n = len(unsorted); assume O(1) comparisons and swaps.
rationale: Time: Heap construction by repeated heapify is O(n) in this implementation’s bottom-up build, followed by n root removals; each recursive heapify descends at most O(log n), giving O(n log n) total. Auxiliary space: The list is sorted in place. Recursive heapify uses at most the heap height, O(log n), stack frames. Owner review: The bottom-up build is O(n), and the n−1 extractions each call heapify, which descends at most O(log n). Total is O(n log n). heapify recurses once per level with no TCO, so the stack is O(log n) and nothing else is allocated.

assumptions: Analyze find and its recursive helper, not the interactive main method. Input array is non-null, sorted under the comparator, indexed access and compareTo are O(1); exclude input storage.
input_size: n = array length; sorted input.
rationale: Time: Each recursive call halves the inclusive search interval and does constant work, so there are O(log n) calls. Auxiliary space: The recursive call stack has one frame per halving step, O(log n). Owner review: Each call halves the inclusive range with O(1) work, so time is O(log n). Java does not eliminate tail calls, so the stack reaches O(log n) frames. Analyzing find plus binsear and skipping main is the right scope.

assumptions: Analyze the recursive method for n >= 0; primitive integer addition and comparisons are treated as O(1). Integer overflow does not change the number of calls. The exact Θ(φ^n) note is explanatory; proposed coarse label is O(2^n).
input_size: n is a non-negative integer.
rationale: Time: The recurrence is T(n)=T(n-1)+T(n-2)+O(1), whose tight growth is Θ(φ^n). The conventional coarser class accepted for this packet is O(2^n). Auxiliary space: The deepest recursive chain decreases n by one until the base case, so the stack depth is O(n). Owner review: T(n) = T(n−1) + T(n−2) + O(1) gives Θ(φ^n), which is bounded above by O(2^n). The call chain along n−1 is n deep, so space is O(n). Θ(φ^n) is not Θ(2^n), so O(2^n) is a valid but loose upper bound; the packet accepts it as the coarse class.

assumptions: Analyze matrix_chain_order only. Let d = len(array) >= 2 and M = d - 1 matrices. Treat integer arithmetic and comparisons as O(1). assumptions: Input is a mutable sequence with O(1) indexed reads/writes. Element comparisons are O(1). Exclude the input and returned sequence.
input_size: n = len(collection); assume comparison of two elements is O(1).
rationale: Time: The outer loop runs n-1 times and the inner scan examines the remaining suffix. The total comparisons are (n-1)+(n-2)+...+1 = Θ(n²), independent of input order. Auxiliary space: The algorithm sorts the input sequence in place and uses only a fixed number of index variables and one temporary swap value. Owner review: Confirmed against source: the outer loop runs n−1 times and the inner scan examines each remaining suffix, producing (n−1)+(n−2)+…+1 = Θ(n²) comparisons for every input order. The in-place swaps use only fixed scalar state, so auxiliary space is O(1).

assumptions: Start with index=0, number_of_items=n, max_weight>=0, and valid weights/values lists. Treat integer operations and list indexing as O(1). The exponential label is the worst case (for example, capacity is at least the sum of all nonnegative item weights); pruning can reduce work on other inputs.
input_size: n = number_of_items; weights and values each contain at least n entries.
rationale: Time: For each item, the function always explores the exclude branch and explores the include branch when it fits. When all include branches remain feasible, the recursion tree has 2^n leaves; work per node is constant. Auxiliary space: The recursion advances index by one on every call, so the deepest call chain has at most n+1 frames. No memoization table is allocated. Owner review: Confirmed against source: there is no memoization or table. The exclude branch always recurses and the include branch recurses when the item fits, giving O(2ⁿ) worst-case calls when all branches remain feasible. The recursion depth is at most n+1, so auxiliary space is O(n).

assumptions: Analyze merge_sort on a list of comparable values with O(1) comparisons. Python list pop(0) shifts the remaining references and costs O(k) for a list of length k. Exclude the input and returned list from auxiliary space; count recursive slices and intermediate merge lists.
expected_auxiliary_space_exact: O(n) excluding input and returned list
input_size: n = len(collection); assume element comparisons are O(1).
rationale: Owner-reviewed time and auxiliary-space rationale: The labels remain O(n²) time and O(n) auxiliary space; this revision corrects assumptions and rationale only. In a merge of two non-empty halves, one half is eventually exhausted by repeated pop(0) calls. The shifts from removing all elements of that half sum to Θ(n²) for the top-level merge regardless of input order, so T(n)=2T(n/2)+Θ(n²)=Θ(n²). Excluding input and returned output, recursion slices and intermediate lists use O(n) peak auxiliary storage. The source docstring says O(n log n), but that claim omits list.pop(0) shifting costs.

assumptions: Both strings are non-null. assumptions: Analyze valid input with vl and wt equal in length n, n matching that length, positive weights, and O(1) arithmetic/comparisons. Exclude input and scalar output.

assumptions: Analyze one call on a DAG with dense vertex IDs 0..V-1, valid adjacency endpoints, a fresh all-zero visited list of length V, and an empty module-global stack. Reset these states before a repeated call. Each vertex is marked before descent. The recursive implementation may exceed Python recursion limits on deep graphs; scoring uses n=V+E.

rationale: Time: With a zeroed visited list, the driver starts DFS once per unvisited vertex. Each vertex is marked before descent and each adjacency entry is checked once, so work is O(V+E). Owner review: Each vertex is marked before descent and each adjacency entry is checked once, so time is O(V+E). The recursive call stack alone can reach V frames, so auxiliary space is O(V); the global stack also grows to O(V) as result storage and does not change the bound. A repeated call with already-marked visited state skips prior vertices. Deep graphs can fail at the Python recursion limit.

assumptions: Analyze the reachable graph with nonnegative edge weights, valid adjacency keys and endpoints, and expected O(1) hash operations. Node labels must be hashable and mutually orderable when equal-cost heap tuples are compared. Treat arithmetic as O(1).
input_size: V = vertices, E = adjacency entries; n = V + E.
rationale: Time: Each settled vertex scans its adjacency list once. Every successful relaxation pushes one heap entry, so there are O(E) pushes and pops, each O(log(E+1)); initialization and graph scans add O(V+E). The implementation may stop earlier when it reaches the destination. Auxiliary space: The cost map and visited set use O(V); stale duplicate heap entries can make the heap O(E). Exclude the input graph. Owner review: Confirmed against the source: each reachable vertex is settled once and each of its adjacency entries is scanned once. Strictly improving relaxations cause at most E+1 heap entries, each push/pop costing O(log(E+1)); initialization and traversal add O(V+E). Time is O(V+E log(E+1)). The costs map and visited set use O(V), and the lazy heap can hold O(E), giving O(V+E) auxiliary space. Module-level demonstration calls are outside the dijkstra entrypoint.

assumptions: Analyze ite_ternary_search only, on an array sorted in ascending order, with module precision fixed independently of n and O(1) comparisons/indexing. The file also contains a separate recursive implementation, which is not the selected entrypoint.
input_size: n = len(array); precision is the module constant 10.
rationale: Each branch reduces the active interval to about one third: the lower third, middle third, or upper third. Thus the loop takes O(log n) iterations. The fixed precision tail examines at most 9 elements. The iterative entrypoint uses O(1) auxiliary space. This review covers ite_ternary_search only, not the separate recursive implementation.

assumptions: For nonempty strings of lengths m and k, the method fills the m×k interior of a table allocated with (m+1)(k+1) cells. An empty input returns in O(1). Character comparison/indexing are O(1). Let n=max(m,k); the coarse O(n²) class is a valid upper bound for all lengths and is tight when m and k are comparable. rationale: Time: For nonempty strings the nested loops fill all m×k interior cells. The final substring slice is O(min(m,k)), dominated by O(mk). The coarse n² class assumes m and k are of comparable order, with n=max(m,k). Auxiliary space: The DP table has (m+1)(k+1) cells. The returned substring uses at most O(min(m,k)) additional space, dominated by the table for nonempty strings. The returned substring uses O(min(m,k)) space but is output and excluded; the table dominates. Empty input returns in O(1). The coarse O(n²) class with n=max(m,k) is an upper bound even for unbalanced lengths, and is tight when lengths are comparable.

assumptions: Score worst-case time and space. Pivot selection, comparisons, and list operations are O(1) per element. Expected-case notes assume uniformly random pivot ranks and distinct values. assumptions: Analyze a valid V×V adjacency matrix with nonnegative weights, 0 meaning no edge, valid source, and O(1) primitive and heap-node comparisons. Let E be the nonzero matrix entries and n=V+E. Each settled vertex scans a full matrix row. Exclude the input matrix and returned distances array from auxiliary space. Include the O(V) output printing in runtime; it is dominated.

rationale: Owner-reviewed time and auxiliary-space rationale: The exact runtime is O(V² + E log(E+1)): up to V processed vertices each scan a full matrix row, and up to E successful relaxations create heap entries with O(log(E+1)) push/pop cost. Printing adds O(V), dominated. With n=V+E the correct coarse time class is O(n²), tight for sparse connected graphs; O(n log n) would miss the V² scan cost. assumptions: Analyze minimumCoins, not change. Amount A≥1 and denominations are positive; C≥1. Use n=max(A,C) for coarse scoring and treat fixed-width integer operations as O(1). Exclude input and scalar output.

rationale: Time: The method initializes A+1 entries, then for each of A positive amounts scans all C coin denominations. Time is O(A*C + A); for A,C≤n this is O(n²). Auxiliary space: The single minimumCoins array has A+1 integer entries, so auxiliary space is O(A), bounded by O(n). Under n=max(A,C), the coarse classes O(n²) time and O(n) space are valid. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial in numeric amount A.
